The gate-walk shows how Thornwater closes; the board and map turn work into a search method; Oryn's delay accumulates as route debt; the report climbs through forms and folders; and the new power's moral law becomes a consent procedure entered in the log.

There is no present fight, exactly as prohibited. The noncombat set pieces remain memorably choreographed and terrain is load-bearing: the wall permits side-by-side disclosure toward the road, six fixed seats turn the common-room table into an evidence circle, and the well isolates the consent covenant. Its win is writable in the requested form: Oryn removed Cael's ability to treat unnoticed contact-reading as harmless curiosity by binding it to an ask-first rule he must encounter with every inventory.

The recalled Ring set piece also survives clearly enough to preserve its tactical receipt: Cael removed the pack's ability to exploit Pathless prey inside the Quiet by becoming the only declaration it could follow across the line. The Lira scene pays six books of trust without turning into an affection declaration. Her covenant answer, fighter's cost question, and good hand against Cael's boot carry emotional movement through procedure, competence, and contact.

The circle differentiates all six by competence. Brom reports weight and cost, Karis controls evidence, Seln supplies the institutional clock, Oryn limits her clinical claim, and Lira confirms from closest range; unanimity emerges through distinct methods rather than matching speeches.

The temptation is concrete and morally losable. A wrist one foot from Cael's hand gives the risk a repeatable physical trigger, while 'the days I don't notice I've started' makes the rule protect against habit rather than melodramatic intent.
